hard_battery.note: the no-lane population the labeled battery cannot represent — unlabeled, so scored by RESCUE RATE (does grounding move a collapsed prompt off the degenerate magnet?) AND by landing diversity, because a rescue that sends every prompt to one domain is a constant function: the injected text decided it. Off-magnet is necessary, spread is what makes it real.

verdict: BATTERY SATURATED — the ungrounded baseline already routes 22/22. This battery CANNOT measure what grounding buys; every level reads identical by construction. The cost side stays real (separation falls monotonically with cap), so on present evidence a SMALLER cap is better — but that conclusion rests on an unmeasured benefit, and the honest next step is a HARDER battery with headroom, not a cap change.
honest_limit: n=22 labeled prompts. One prompt = 4.5pp, so only multi-prompt gaps mean anything. Measures ROUTING accuracy only — not answer quality, not enrichment usefulness. A saturated baseline makes every row uninformative regardless of n.
what_would_measure_it: a battery of prompts the ungrounded lens gets WRONG — deictic fragments (the 18 no-lane prompts already catalogued in unenriched-report.json are exactly this population), or prompts whose ideal domain is a near-neighbour of where they place ungrounded. Until such a battery exists, the grounding cap is an un-derivable judgment and must stay labelled as one.
